blocks.content: The rock cycle is the continuous process through which rocks transform from one type to another over geological time.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The rock cycle is a continuous geological process transforming rocks from one type to another.
Weathered rock particles compact to form sedimentary rocks.
Heat and pressure transform rocks into metamorphic rocks.
Metamorphic rocks can melt back into magma, continuing the cycle indefinitely.

blocks.content: The rock cycle demonstrates that no rock type is permanent.
• Magma cools to form igneous rocks.
• Sediments compact to form sedimentary rocks.
• Heat and pressure convert rocks into metamorphic rocks.

items: Heat and pressure are key factors specifically required for forming metamorphic rocks.
Sedimentary rock formation relies on the sequential processes of weathering and sediment compaction.
No rock type is permanent in geological time; any rock type can revert to magma or convert to another form.

blocks.content: • Metamorphic rocks may melt again to form magma.
The rock cycle demonstrates that no rock type is permanent.
